# Compatibility fixtures

## Encryption

These five small PDFs exercise the Standard Security Handler revisions 2–6:

- RC4 with 40-bit and 128-bit keys;
- AES-128 with object-specific keys;
- AES-256 revisions 5 and 6.

They were generated by `generate_encrypted_fixtures.py` with pypdf 6.10.0 and
ReportLab 4.4.9, then opened independently with Poppler command-line tools.
The generators are not runtime or build dependencies of Poppler.Net.

`verify_encrypted_fixtures.py` checks every manifest hash and independently
recovers the expected metadata, text and attachment bytes.

The files use user password `user-03` and owner password `owner-03`. The user
permission mask allows printing, copying and accessibility extraction while
denying modification, annotations, forms and document assembly.

Four AES-128 variants additionally cover different `StrF`/`StmF` selections,
an independent `EFF`, an explicit stream `/Crypt` filter and the
`EncryptMetadata false` file-key branch.

## Embedded fonts

`truetype-cmap-fallback.pdf` and `opentype-cff-cmap-fallback.pdf` contain tiny
subsets for `ABC`, a custom `CIDToGIDMap`, and deliberately omit `ToUnicode`.
They exercise the managed sfnt cmap fallback for CID TrueType and CID Type 0C
OpenType fonts.

`generate_font_fixtures.py` recreates them with FontTools. Poppler command-line
tools and pypdf 6.10.0 independently recover `ABC`; `pdffonts` identifies both files as
embedded subsets without `ToUnicode`. `font-fixtures.json` records their
hashes and [FONT_LICENSES.md](FONT_LICENSES.md) records font provenance.

`rendering-beta1.pdf` is generated by
`generate_beta1_text_corpus.py`. Its four pages exercise a synthetic OpenType
CFF2 program, an inherited external vertical CMap with GSUB alternates, an
exact multi-scalar `fi` ligature in a controlled substitute font and
Narrow/Condensed family matching. `rendering-beta1-fixture.json` records the
PDF, CMap and font hashes; `beta-fonts/` and `cmaps/` are deterministic,
application-controlled test resources.

## Graphics

`graphics-engine.pdf` is a dependency-free deterministic fixture generated by
`generate_graphics_fixture.py`. It contains path fills/strokes, a persistent
clip bounded by `q`/`Q`, common `ExtGState` values, a transformed Form XObject,
Image XObject metadata, a colored tiling pattern, a radial shading pattern and
a directly painted axial shading.

`graphics-fixture.json` records its hash and coverage. Poppler 26.07.0
successfully parses the page and `pdftocairo` renders a 420×400 reference image.

## Rendering and transparency

`rendering-transparency.pdf` is generated without a third-party PDF library by
`generate_rendering_fixture.py`. Its first page covers Multiply, constant
alpha, Alpha and Luminosity soft masks, an isolated Form transparency group and
clipping. Its second page covers `/Rotate 90`.

`rendering-fixture.json` records the deterministic hash and output dimensions.
At 72 DPI the managed raster samples are compared with Poppler 26.05.0 output,
including the isolated-group overlap and both soft-mask paths.

`rendering-beta2.pdf` is generated by
`generate_beta2_graphics_corpus.py` without a third-party PDF library. Its six
pages cover free-form/lattice Gouraud meshes, Coons/tensor-product patch
meshes, per-use colors on one uncolored pattern resource, a calculator
soft-mask transfer, isolated/non-isolated/knockout groups and process overprint
mode 1. `rendering-beta2-fixture.json` records the deterministic hash.
Raster references use Poppler at 72 DPI; its overprint page is generated with
the explicit `-overprint` option.

## Annotations

`annotations-alpha1.pdf` is generated by
`generate_alpha1_annotation_corpus.py` without a third-party PDF library. Its
four pages cover URI, direct and name-tree links; annotation flags; normal
appearance streams and state dictionaries; rotated appearance matrices;
nested and recursive Forms; note, FreeText, markup and shape fallbacks; and
named destination targets.

`annotations-alpha1-fixture.json` records the deterministic hash. Raster
references use Poppler at 72 DPI with 2x vector/text antialiasing. Explicit
appearances are compared geometrically; missing-appearance fallbacks are
classified separately because their visual style is viewer-defined.
